submitted.rationale: Index 71 (Bi0.10 Cu0.49 V0.41), a Cu-vanadate composition with a little Bi, had the highest measured photocurrent: 8.1e-7 A. The other two measurements were 3.1e-7 A and 4.2e-7 A. The foundation-model calls only worked on binary oxides because the ternary phase ids couldn't be retrieved. Those results only broadly suggested that Cu is needed to absorb light at 2.4 eV.

rejected.reason: BiVO4-like with little Cu; measured 3.1e-7 A, lower photocurrent, probably because its gap is close to the 2.4 eV photon energy
Slightly more Cu and less Bi than 71; measured 4.2e-7 A, lower than 71

consultations.verdict: Weak support / largely uninformative for ternaries: MEGNet HSE gaps Cu2O 1.56, V2O5 2.83, CuO 0.32 eV. V-oxide gap exceeds 2.4 eV photon energy, so pure-vanadate/BiVO4-like phases need Cu (d-states lowering gap) to absorb; Cu-rich oxides have small gaps but poor photoanode behavior (CuO narrow gap, p-type). Index 3 (Bi0.40 Cu0.19 V0.41) is BiVO4-like with moderate Cu, a plausible balance of absorption at 2.4 eV and n-type photoanode activity. Ternary phases could not be queried (ids unavailable).

Uninformative for the target: MACE confirms V2O5 on hull (-1.37 eV/atom formation), meaning V-oxide end is stable but that says nothing specific about Cu vanadates. Measuring 71 (Bi0.10 Cu0.49 V0.41, Cu-vanadate region, e.g., Cu2V2O7/Cu3V2O8 with gaps ~2 eV that absorb at 2.4 eV) to explore a distinct region from index 3 (3.1e-7 A).

Uninformative-to-mild: Cu2O PBE gap 0.59 eV (HSE 1.56) reiterates that Cu lowers the gap, consistent with the observed trend (Cu-richer 71 at 8.1e-7 A > BiVO4-like 3 at 3.1e-7 A). Measuring 37 (Bi0.089 Cu0.519 V0.391), which continues the trend toward less Bi and more Cu while keeping Cu:V near the Cu-vanadate range.
